title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): an exact sequence of discrete groups 1 → M → G → H → 1, with M commutative. The case of interest is M a free Z-module of finite type, with H acting on M by conjugation. M defines the group functor M̲ : A ↦ M⊗_Z A over S0 = Spec Z. For M free of rank r this is the vector group G_a^r, smooth of finite type. Grothendieck wants group objects G̲ and H̲ = H_{S0} (the constant group) over S0, an exact sequence 1 → M̲ → G̲ → H̲ → 1, and an isomorphism of this sequence on Z-points with the original one.

On this page he proposes the naive definition (30): G̲(A) = G ∧^M (M⊗_Z A). This is the pushout of the extension G along the H-equivariant homomorphism (31) M → M⊗_Z A, where H acts on M⊗A through its action on M. Concretely it is (G ⋉ (M⊗A)) / {(m, −m⊗1)}, an extension of H by M⊗A. It is covariant in A, contravariant in S = Spec A over S0.

The 'small difficulty': this functor is not representable (not even a Zariski sheaf). Its H-component is a single element of H, whereas a morphism S → H_S to the constant group is a locally constant H-valued function. For A = A1×A2 the naive functor gives only the pairs with equal H-components, not G̲(A1)×G̲(A2). So (30) is correct only when Spec A is connected. The naive functor is identified with the subfunctor of the 'true' G̲ consisting of the S → G̲ whose composite S → H̲_S (32) is constant.

The next page repairs this by Zariski sheafification: (33) is a colimit over partitions of S into open-and-closed pieces. It then recasts the construction as an instance of a general pushout construction of his §49 in the sheaf setting. The data are the sheaf of groups M̲, the constant group G_{S0} with distinguished subgroup M_{S0}, a homomorphism M_{S0} → M̲, and a compatible action of G on M̲.

The representing object is the disjoint union over h ∈ H of copies of M⊗G_a (affine r-space). It is a smooth group scheme over Z, not of finite type if H is infinite, and an extension of the constant group H by the vector group. Its Q- and Z_l-points give the 'rationalization' or 'l-adic completion along M' of the virtually-abelian-type extension, e.g. for M a characteristic abelian subgroup of a fundamental-group-type group.
errors: No mathematical error. The diagnosis that (30) is not a sheaf and is correct only for connected Spec A is right, and the sheafification via partitions into clopen pieces (next page) is the right fix.

Possible slip in the transcribed wording of (32): the naive functor corresponds to maps S → G̲ whose composite to H̲_S is constant, not 'locally constant'. Every map to a constant group scheme is already locally constant, so the insertion 'localement' would make the condition vacuous. The image should be rechecked.

ideas.what: Pushout of a group extension along an H-equivariant map of the abelian kernel: G ∧^M M'
ideas.modern_name: pushout/induced extension (change of coefficients in H^2(H, M))
ideas.where_published: standard; contracted products ∧ appear in SGA 1/SGA 3/Giraud-style nonabelian cohomology

ideas.what: Group scheme over Z extending the constant group H by the vector group M⊗G_a, whose Z-points recover the discrete extension G
ideas.modern_name: algebraic hull / relative (Malcev-type) completion of a virtually abelian extension; base change of a discrete group to a group scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev (rational completions); relative completion: Deligne, Hain (1990s)
ideas.where_published: unsure; the surrounding Longue Marche continuation is unpublished

ideas.what: Naive functor A ↦ G∧^M(M⊗A) is not a Zariski sheaf because of the constant-group component; fix by Zariski sheafification over clopen partitions
ideas.modern_name: sheafification; constant group scheme as locally constant functions

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, carefully stated technical step: the base change of a discrete group extension to a group scheme over Spec Z, with the standard non-sheaf issue. It is a building block toward something in the unpublished §49-onwards material, but nothing on this page is new or unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: '(comm.)' written above 'foncteur' is more likely '(cov.)' (covariant), pairing with '(contravariant) en S/S0'.
'n'est pas lim = représentable' should read 'n'est pas représentable'.
'Il correspond au ~-foncteur de' is likely 'Il correspond au sous-foncteur de S ↦ G̲(S)'.
In (32), the condition is probably 'soit constante'; the superscript insertion read as 'localement' should be rechecked, since 'locally constant' would be vacuous.
In (30), the subscript is the struck-out 'M⊗_Z' followed by 'M⊗_Z A', i.e. G ∧^M (M⊗_Z A) with M(A) := M⊗_Z A.
